title: TN SB1624: AN ACT to amend Tennessee Code Annotated, Title 2, Chapter 19, relative to the Transparency for Deepfakes in Political Advertising Act.

obligations: An audio communication that is a deepfake as defined in § 39-17-1902 and impersonates a candidate for elected office engaging in speech the candidate did not in fact engage in must clearly state at the beginning and at the end: "This communication contains fake content impersonating speech that did not occur." (Section 2, subdivision (a)(6)(A))

A video communication that is a deepfake as defined in § 39-17-1902 and depicts a candidate for elected office engaging in action or speech the depicted candidate did not in fact engage in must clearly state in large letters for the duration of the video: if only video media, "This communication contains fake content depicting actions that did not occur."; if both audio and video media, "This communication contains fake content depicting actions and speech that did not occur." (Section 2, subdivision (a)(6)(B))

For a non-incumbent candidate, the disclaimer requirements apply only if the communication is distributed within one hundred twenty (120) days of the initiation of voting in an election in which the candidate appears on the ballot. (Section 2, subdivision (a)(6)(C))
prohibitions: Not stated in the text as an express prohibition; the act imposes affirmative disclaimer requirements on covered communications rather than stating a separate prohibition. (Section 2)

If acting as a platform, ISP, search engine, cloud provider, or broadcaster, ensure you are not responsible for creation of the deepfake to qualify for the liability exemption. (Section 2, subdivision (a)(6)(D))

Passed 2026-03-30. Reading generated by ollama:deepseek-v4-pro from the enrolled text; the full text is at the foot of this page so every statement can be checked against it. LegiScan record · official text

What it does

The act requires disclaimers on audio and video communications that are deepfakes impersonating or depicting a candidate for elected office in political advertising. It provides liability exemptions for certain internet platforms and broadcasters that did not create the deepfake, and gives the depicted candidate a right to damages and equitable relief. It takes effect July 1, 2026.

Who it applies to

  • Any person or entity that creates or distributes a communication in audio or video form that is a deepfake impersonating or depicting a candidate for elected office (Section 2, subdivision (a)(6))
  • Hosts, third-party producers, internet service providers, search engines, and cloud service providers, but only to the extent they are not responsible for creation of the deepfake (Section 2, subdivision (a)(6)(D)(1))
  • Radio or television broadcasting stations, cable or satellite television operators, streaming or other programming services when paid to broadcast material containing a deepfake, to the extent not responsible for creation (Section 2, subdivision (a)(6)(D)(2))
  • Candidates for elected office who are impersonated or depicted in a deepfake communication (Section 2, subdivision (a)(6)(E))

Effective date

July 1, 2026 (Section 3)

Key definitions

  • deepfake: as defined in § 39-17-1902 (Section 2, subdivision (a)(6))

Obligations

  • An audio communication that is a deepfake as defined in § 39-17-1902 and impersonates a candidate for elected office engaging in speech the candidate did not in fact engage in must clearly state at the beginning and at the end: "This communication contains fake content impersonating speech that did not occur." (Section 2, subdivision (a)(6)(A))
  • A video communication that is a deepfake as defined in § 39-17-1902 and depicts a candidate for elected office engaging in action or speech the depicted candidate did not in fact engage in must clearly state in large letters for the duration of the video: if only video media, "This communication contains fake content depicting actions that did not occur."; if both audio and video media, "This communication contains fake content depicting actions and speech that did not occur." (Section 2, subdivision (a)(6)(B))
  • For a non-incumbent candidate, the disclaimer requirements apply only if the communication is distributed within one hundred twenty (120) days of the initiation of voting in an election in which the candidate appears on the ballot. (Section 2, subdivision (a)(6)(C))

Prohibitions

  • Not stated in the text as an express prohibition; the act imposes affirmative disclaimer requirements on covered communications rather than stating a separate prohibition. (Section 2)

Penalties and enforcement

The impersonated or depicted candidate for elected office is entitled to damages and equitable relief as provided in § 39-17-1904, except § 39-17-1904(c) (Section 2, subdivision (a)(6)(E)). No other enforcement authority or penalties are stated in this act. Private right of action is available to the depicted candidate only.

How it affects AI deployment

  • An organisation deploying AI to create or distribute audio deepfakes of a candidate in political advertising must add the exact disclaimer at the beginning and end of the audio. (Section 2, subdivision (a)(6)(A))
  • An organisation deploying AI to create or distribute video deepfakes must display the exact disclaimer in large letters for the entire duration of the video, using the video-only or combined audio/video text as applicable. (Section 2, subdivision (a)(6)(B))
  • If the candidate is not an incumbent, the organisation must check whether distribution occurs within 120 days of the initiation of voting; outside that window the disclaimer requirement does not apply. (Section 2, subdivision (a)(6)(C))
  • Platforms, ISPs, search engines, cloud providers, and broadcasters that merely provide access, connection, transmission, or paid broadcast and did not create the deepfake are not liable under this subdivision. (Section 2, subdivision (a)(6)(D))
  • The depicted candidate can sue the organisation for damages and equitable relief under § 39-17-1904, except § 39-17-1904(c). (Section 2, subdivision (a)(6)(E))

Notable exemptions

  • A host, third-party producer, or internet service provider, including affiliates or subsidiaries, or an operator of a search engine or cloud service provider, is not liable solely for providing access or connection to or from a website or other internet content, or for transmission, downloading, intermediate storage, or access software, to the extent not responsible for creation of the deceptive and fraudulent deepfake. (Section 2, subdivision (a)(6)(D)(1))
  • A radio or television broadcasting station, cable or satellite television operator, streaming or other programming service when paid to broadcast material containing a deepfake is not liable to the extent it is not responsible for creation of the deceptive and fraudulent deepfake. (Section 2, subdivision (a)(6)(D)(2))
  • For a non-incumbent candidate, the disclaimer requirements apply only within 120 days of the initiation of voting in an election in which the candidate appears on the ballot. (Section 2, subdivision (a)(6)(C))

Compliance steps

  • Determine whether the communication is a deepfake as defined in § 39-17-1902 and impersonates or depicts a candidate for elected office engaging in speech or action that did not occur. (Section 2, subdivision (a)(6))
  • Identify whether the candidate is an incumbent office holder; if not, confirm the communication is distributed within 120 days of the initiation of voting in the relevant election. (Section 2, subdivision (a)(6)(C))
  • For audio communications, include the exact disclaimer at the beginning and at the end. (Section 2, subdivision (a)(6)(A))
  • For video-only communications, display the exact disclaimer in large letters for the duration of the video. (Section 2, subdivision (a)(6)(B)(i))
  • For communications with both audio and video, display the combined disclaimer in large letters for the duration of the video. (Section 2, subdivision (a)(6)(B)(ii))
  • If acting as a platform, ISP, search engine, cloud provider, or broadcaster, ensure you are not responsible for creation of the deepfake to qualify for the liability exemption. (Section 2, subdivision (a)(6)(D))

 PUBLIC CHAPTER NO. 625
 HOUSE BILL NO. 1513

 By Representatives Zachary, Russell, Davis, McCalmon, Clemmons, Powell

 Substituted for: Senate Bill No. 1624

 By Senators Massey, Campbell, Bowling, Haile, Yarbro

 AN ACT to amend Tennessee Code Annotated, Title 2, Chapter 19, relative to the
Transparency for Deepfakes in Political Advertising Act.

BE IT ENACTED BY THE GENERAL ASSEMBLY OF THE STATE OF TENNESSEE:

 SECTION 1. This act is known and may be cited as the "Transparency for Deepfakes in
Political Advertising Act."

 SECTION 2. Tennessee Code Annotated, Section 2-19-120(a), is amended by adding
the following as a new subdivision:

 (6)

 (A) Such communication, when in audio form, if considered a deepfake as
 defined in § 39-17-1902 and impersonating a candidate for elected office
 engaging in speech in which the candidate did not in fact engage, shall clearly
 state at the beginning and at the end of the communication:

 This communication contains fake content impersonating speech
 that did not occur.

 (B) Such communication, when in video form, if considered a deepfake as
 defined in § 39-17-1902 and depicting a candidate for elected office engaging in
 action or speech in which the depicted candidate did not in fact engage, shall
 clearly state in large letters for the duration of the video:

 (i) If the communication includes only video media:

 This communication contains fake content depicting
 actions that did not occur.

 (ii) If the communication includes both audio and video media of a
 candidate engaging in action or speech in which the candidate did not
 engage:

 This communication contains fake content depicting
 actions and speech that did not occur.

 (C) When the impersonated or depicted candidate is not an incumbent
 office holder, subdivisions {a)(6)(A) and (a)(6)(B) apply only if the communication
 is distributed within one hundred twenty (120) days of the initiation of voting in an
 election in which the candidate for elected office appears on the ballot.

 (D)

 (1) A person or entity that is a host, third-party producer, or
 internet service provider, including its affiliates or subsidiaries, or that
 operates a search engine or a cloud service provider, is not liable under
 this subdivision (a)(6) solely for providing access or connection to or from
 a website or other information or content on the internet, nor is a facility,
 system, or network not under the control of the internet service provider
 liable under this subdivision (a)(6), including from transmission,

 downloading, intermediate storage, or access software, to the extent such
 provider is not responsible for the creation of the deceptive and fraudulent
 deepfake.

 (2) This subdivision (a)(6) does not apply to a radio or television
 broadcasting station, cable or satellite television operator, streaming or
 other programming service when it is paid to broadcast material
 containing a deepfake, to the extent such entity is not responsible for the
 creation of the deceptive and fraudulent deepfake.

 (E) An impersonated or depicted candidate for elected office who is the
 subject of a deepfake communication as described in this subdivision (a)(6) is
 entitled to damages and equitable relief as provided for in§ 39-17-1904, with the
 exception of§ 39-17-1904(c).

 SECTION 3. This act takes effect July 1, 2026, the public welfare requiring it.
